Principal Product Marketing Manager, AI Governance
Regulatory Counsel, AI Regulation, US
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY

reading.body:
Major AI companies are hiring for compute and infrastructure policy roles, signaling that regulatory clarity around compute access and power allocation is becoming a core business function rather than a legal afterthought.

The four posted roles span companies with different positions in the AI stack. Cohere and Anthropic are hiring for regulatory and policy roles explicitly tied to compute and infrastructure. Databricks and ServiceNow are hiring for AI governance functions that touch cost management and resource allocation. All four postings are recent, clustered between April and September 2026. This suggests compute policy is not a static compliance matter but an active, evolving priority.

The titles reveal what companies believe will be contested: access to compute, infrastructure sovereignty, and the financial governance of AI systems. A role focused on "Compute, Infrastructure & Sovereign AI" at Cohere, for instance, assumes these questions will be negotiated with governments and stakeholders. The emphasis on governance across multiple companies indicates no single technical or market solution has settled the question of how compute will be allocated or regulated.

This data does not show what policies are actually being shaped, whether hiring is accelerating or declining, or how policy priorities differ between companies. The sourcing comes from company career boards and aggregators, capturing visible postings but not total headcount or internal team size. It reflects what companies choose to publicize, not the full scope of policy work underway.
